scenario.description: A disruption to global crude supply raises oil prices; transmission to India via import costs, inflation, the rupee and energy-intensive sectors.
limitations: Supply-driven and demand-driven oil moves are not distinguished by the model.
Indian retail fuel prices are partly administered; pass-through to OMCs depends on policy.

edges.mechanism: Initiating entity named by the scenario definition.
User assumption: Crude oil price change +60% over 5 trading sessions

evidence.summary: User assumption: Crude oil price change +60% over 5 trading sessions

edges.mechanism: Jet fuel / ATF is refined from crude, so its price tracks crude plus a refining crack spread.

evidence.summary: Jet fuel / ATF is refined from crude, so its price tracks crude plus a refining crack spread. Rationale: Refined product prices are anchored to crude input costs.

edges.conditions_note: Crack spreads and (in India) ATF taxation modify pass-through.

edges.mechanism: India imports most of the crude it consumes, so a higher price raises the import bill for given volumes.

evidence.summary: India imports most of the crude it consumes, so a higher price raises the import bill for given volumes. Rationale: Import bill = price x volume; India is a large net crude importer.

edges.conditions_note: Applies globally because India is a price-taker; strongest relevance when the event involves India.

edges.mechanism: Fuel and transport costs feed into consumer prices directly and via second-round effects.

evidence.summary: Fuel and transport costs feed into consumer prices directly and via second-round effects. Rationale: Energy weight in CPI and input-cost pass-through.

edges.conditions_note: Retail fuel prices in India are partly administered, which delays pass-through.

edges.mechanism: Gasoline is a component of US CPI, so crude prices pass through to headline inflation.

evidence.summary: Gasoline is a component of US CPI, so crude prices pass through to headline inflation. Rationale: Energy component of headline CPI.

edges.conditions_note: Core inflation is much less sensitive than headline.

edges.mechanism: Producers sell crude at prices linked to benchmarks, so realisations rise with the oil price.

evidence.summary: Producers sell crude at prices linked to benchmarks, so realisations rise with the oil price. Rationale: Revenue = realised price x volume.

edges.conditions_note: Windfall taxes, hedging and production volumes modify the effect.

edges.mechanism: When retail fuel prices are held steady, higher crude costs squeeze state-run OMC marketing margins.

evidence.summary: When retail fuel prices are held steady, higher crude costs squeeze state-run OMC marketing margins. Rationale: Administered-price regime limits pass-through.

edges.conditions_note: Depends on government pricing decisions; margins recover if retail prices are raised.

edges.mechanism: Refining margins depend on the spread between product and crude prices, not the crude level itself.

evidence.summary: Refining margins depend on the spread between product and crude prices, not the crude level itself. Rationale: Crack spreads are driven by product demand and refinery capacity.

edges.conditions_note: Direction is context-dependent: product prices may rise faster or slower than crude.

edges.mechanism: Solvents, monomers and other crude derivatives are priced off crude.

evidence.summary: Solvents, monomers and other crude derivatives are priced off crude. Rationale: Petrochemical feedstocks derive from crude.

edges.conditions_note: Lag of one to two quarters through inventory.

edges.mechanism: Russia is a major crude exporter; higher prices raise export revenue for given volumes.

evidence.summary: Russia is a major crude exporter; higher prices raise export revenue for given volumes. Rationale: Revenue = price x volume for a large exporter.

edges.conditions_note: Sanctions-related discounts and price caps reduce realised prices.

edges.mechanism: Front-month Brent futures price the international crude benchmark directly.

evidence.summary: Front-month Brent futures price the international crude benchmark directly. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Brent crude futures (front month).

edges.mechanism: WTI futures track the US crude benchmark, which co-moves closely with Brent.

evidence.summary: WTI futures track the US crude benchmark, which co-moves closely with Brent. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for WTI crude futures (front month).

edges.mechanism: Fuel is typically one of the largest airline operating-cost items.

evidence.summary: Fuel is typically one of the largest airline operating-cost items. Rationale: Airline cost structures are fuel-intensive.

edges.conditions_note: Fuel hedging delays and dampens the effect.

edges.mechanism: A larger oil import bill widens the trade deficit and hence the current account deficit.

evidence.summary: A larger oil import bill widens the trade deficit and hence the current account deficit. Rationale: Balance-of-payments accounting identity.

edges.conditions_note: Services exports and remittances can offset.

edges.mechanism: Higher inflation reduces the RBI's room to cut and can raise expectations of tighter policy.

evidence.summary: Higher inflation reduces the RBI's room to cut and can raise expectations of tighter policy. Rationale: Inflation-targeting reaction function.

edges.conditions_note: The RBI's flexible inflation-targeting framework also weighs growth.

edges.mechanism: Higher inflation prints lead markets to price a tighter Fed path.

evidence.summary: Higher inflation prints lead markets to price a tighter Fed path. Rationale: Fed dual mandate reaction function.

edges.conditions_note: The Fed focuses on core measures; energy-driven headline moves may be looked through.

edges.mechanism: US energy-sector earnings rise with realised oil prices.

evidence.summary: US energy-sector earnings rise with realised oil prices. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF.

edges.mechanism: Upstream realisations rise with crude prices, subject to windfall taxes and subsidy-sharing policy.

evidence.summary: Upstream realisations rise with crude prices, subject to windfall taxes and subsidy-sharing policy. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (NSE: ONGC).

edges.mechanism: Upstream earnings rise with realised crude prices.

evidence.summary: Upstream earnings rise with realised crude prices. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Exxon Mobil (NYSE: XOM).

edges.mechanism: Upstream earnings rise with realised crude prices.

evidence.summary: Upstream earnings rise with realised crude prices. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Chevron (NYSE: CVX).

edges.mechanism: Fuel-marketing margins drive OMC earnings when retail prices are held steady.

evidence.summary: Fuel-marketing margins drive OMC earnings when retail prices are held steady. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Bharat Petroleum (NSE: BPCL).

edges.mechanism: Marketing-heavy business mix makes earnings sensitive to retail fuel margins.

evidence.summary: Marketing-heavy business mix makes earnings sensitive to retail fuel margins. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Hindustan Petroleum (NSE: HINDPETRO).

edges.mechanism: Integrated refiner-marketer; marketing margins are a key earnings driver.

evidence.summary: Integrated refiner-marketer; marketing margins are a key earnings driver. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Indian Oil Corporation (NSE: IOC).

edges.mechanism: Refining is a major earnings segment, but the group is diversified (telecom, retail).

evidence.summary: Refining is a major earnings segment, but the group is diversified (telecom, retail). Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Reliance Industries (NSE: RELIANCE).

edges.mechanism: Crude-linked raw materials are a meaningful share of paint-makers' costs.

evidence.summary: Crude-linked raw materials are a meaningful share of paint-makers' costs. Rationale: Input-cost sensitivity of decorative paints.

edges.conditions_note: Strong brands can pass costs through with a lag.

edges.mechanism: Higher export earnings raise foreign-currency inflows and support the rouble.

evidence.summary: Higher export earnings raise foreign-currency inflows and support the rouble. Rationale: Terms-of-trade effect on a commodity-exporter currency.

edges.conditions_note: Capital controls and mandatory FX-sale rules distort the relationship.

edges.mechanism: Energy exporters dominate the index.

evidence.summary: Energy exporters dominate the index. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for MOEX Russia Index.

edges.mechanism: Higher costs compress margins unless airlines pass them on through fares or fuel surcharges.

evidence.summary: Higher costs compress margins unless airlines pass them on through fares or fuel surcharges. Rationale: Margin = revenue - costs; incomplete pass-through squeezes margins.

edges.conditions_note: Pass-through depends on demand strength and competition.

edges.mechanism: A wider current account deficit increases dollar demand from importers, pressuring the rupee.

evidence.summary: A wider current account deficit increases dollar demand from importers, pressuring the rupee. Rationale: External financing needs affect currency demand.

edges.conditions_note: RBI FX intervention and capital inflows can offset.

edges.mechanism: Bond yields embed the expected path of policy rates.

evidence.summary: Bond yields embed the expected path of policy rates. Rationale: Expectations hypothesis of the term structure.

edges.conditions_note: Fiscal supply and foreign index inclusion flows also move yields.

edges.mechanism: Treasury yields embed the expected path of the federal funds rate.

evidence.summary: Treasury yields embed the expected path of the federal funds rate. Rationale: Expectations hypothesis of the term structure.

edges.conditions_note: Term premium and safe-haven flows can dominate on the long end.

edges.mechanism: Crude derivatives are a significant raw-material input; pricing power can offset with a lag.

evidence.summary: Crude derivatives are a significant raw-material input; pricing power can offset with a lag. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Asian Paints (NSE: ASIANPAINT).

edges.mechanism: A weaker rouble raises the rouble-per-dollar rate.

evidence.summary: A weaker rouble raises the rouble-per-dollar rate. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for USD/RUB exchange rate.

edges.mechanism: The ETF holds airline equities whose valuations depend on margins.

evidence.summary: The ETF holds airline equities whose valuations depend on margins. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for US Global Jets ETF.

edges.mechanism: Fuel is a large share of Indian airline costs; margin pressure tends to weigh on the stock.

evidence.summary: Fuel is a large share of Indian airline costs; margin pressure tends to weigh on the stock. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for InterGlobe Aviation (NSE: INDIGO).

edges.mechanism: Jet fuel is a major airline cost; hedging and refinery ownership can partially offset.

evidence.summary: Jet fuel is a major airline cost; hedging and refinery ownership can partially offset. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for Delta Air Lines (NYSE: DAL).

edges.mechanism: Jet fuel is a major, largely unhedged airline cost.

evidence.summary: Jet fuel is a major, largely unhedged airline cost. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for United Airlines Holdings (NASDAQ: UAL).

edges.mechanism: Jet fuel is a major airline cost and the company is highly leveraged.

evidence.summary: Jet fuel is a major airline cost and the company is highly leveraged. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for American Airlines Group (NASDAQ: AAL).

edges.mechanism: USD/INR is quoted as rupees per dollar, so a weaker rupee shows up as a higher USD/INR rate.

evidence.summary: USD/INR is quoted as rupees per dollar, so a weaker rupee shows up as a higher USD/INR rate. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for USD/INR exchange rate.

edges.mechanism: The instrument is the benchmark Indian sovereign yield itself.

evidence.summary: The instrument is the benchmark Indian sovereign yield itself. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for India 10-year government bond yield.

edges.mechanism: The instrument is the benchmark 10-year yield itself.

evidence.summary: The instrument is the benchmark 10-year yield itself. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for US 10-year Treasury yield (CBOE ^TNX).

edges.mechanism: Bond prices move inversely to yields; long duration amplifies the effect.

evidence.summary: Bond prices move inversely to yields; long duration amplifies the effect. Rationale: Asset exposure declared in the asset catalog for iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF.

model.interpretation: Conditional association: estimated 5-session return of each Indian target GIVEN the specified shocks occur over the same 5 sessions, from 2016-2026 weekly history. Not a forecast; not causal.
model.return_unit: % simple return over 5 NSE trading sessions

evaluation.method: walk-forward by target-end year 2019..2026 (fit on earlier years only)

limitations: Assumes the shocks happen within the same 5 trading sessions as the return; unspecified shocks are held at 0 change (an explicit scenario assumption).
Linear model: responses scale linearly; behaviour outside the training range is extrapolation and is refused by the backend.
Fitted mostly on ordinary weeks (411 of 493 are NORMAL); only 2 independent Black Swan episodes exist in the data.
Intervals come from historical residuals and assume similar error behaviour; they are not guarantees.
No inflation input exists; inflation sliders cannot affect this model.

model_compatibility.reason: Its shock inputs describe the PAST 5 sessions. A slider describing a hypothetical future move cannot be fed into them without changing their meaning; on the 2023-2026 test it does not beat the zero or training-mean baselines.

Inputs are trailing 5-session moves; a hypothetical shock can only be read as 'the shock already happened last week', which excludes the immediate reaction. The model also shows no skill: its test MAE is not distinguishable from the zero-return baseline.
